methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR consensus cheat sheet checked Aug. 30
ESPN 2026 PPR draft guide and current analyst rankings through Aug. 30
RotoWire PPR cheat sheet updated Aug. 29/30, including expert dispersion and injury flags
Rotoworld/NBC Sports Top 200 published Aug. 26 and Yahoo 2026 draft kit checked Aug. 30
CBS Sports current PPR ADP/model coverage and NFL roster/injury reporting through Aug. 30
methodology.marketInput: Current PPR ADP remains a separate market-price input, cross-checked across CBS, FantasyPros and platform-market references. ADP is not used as a substitute for player value; large gaps are preserved when news risk or expert disagreement justifies them.
newsInputs: The top of the board is reordered to Jahmyr Gibbs No. 1, Bijan Robinson No. 2 and Ja'Marr Chase No. 3. RotoWire and Rotoworld independently have that exact top three, while CBS PPR ADP is Gibbs 1, Bijan 2 and Chase 3. This is now the strongest cross-source center rather than an ADP-only move.

Saquon Barkley moves materially upward from No. 27 to No. 18. RotoWire currently ranks him No. 15 and Rotoworld No. 12, while multi-platform ADP is roughly the mid-teens. The prior No. 27 value had drifted too far below both independent expert value and market price.

Ashton Jeanty remains discounted relative to market because of the ankle issue and role uncertainty. RotoWire is substantially more aggressive at No. 19 while Rotoworld is No. 29, so the wide expert range is preserved rather than forcing false precision.
Kenneth Walker III remains inside the top 25 despite the swollen ankle because current reporting continues to describe the issue as minor; RotoWire still ranks him No. 18 while flagging the ankle.
No other Aug. 30 roster cut, trade, suspension, depth-chart or preseason development justified a larger top-30 move in the public board.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertHigh/expertLow ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.

players.name: Ja'Marr Chase
players.news: Moves from No. 1 to No. 3 as the freshest cross-source center now has Gibbs and Bijan ahead. Chase remains the clear WR1 on several boards and stays inside the elite top-three tier.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.news: Still an elite PPR value, but confidence remains reduced by the recent groin designation and unresolved discipline risk. Current independent boards still place him roughly No. 4 overall, so the baseline rank holds while the downside range stays wide.

players.name: Omarion Hampton
players.news: RotoWire has Hampton No. 14 overall and current model-driven breakout support remains strong. Market cost still sits later, preserving a modest value edge.

players.name: Saquon Barkley
players.news: Major upward correction from No. 27. RotoWire ranks him No. 15 and Rotoworld No. 12, while current platform ADP is roughly 14-16. The old value rank was too bearish relative to both expert value and market price.

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.news: RotoWire still ranks him No. 18 while flagging the ankle. Current reporting describes the swelling as minor, so the board preserves top-20 value with a wide downside range.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.news: Still intentionally discounted versus market. RotoWire is aggressive at No. 19 while Rotoworld is No. 29, and the ankle plus possible two-back usage keeps the disagreement unusually wide.
